approach: The drain already continues past every self-stopping item, so no behavior changes. Evidence, all in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: `attempts` returns Paused, Awaiting, Flagged, Failed, NeedsAccepting, Held, Skipped and Waiting at lines 1963-2053 and none of them sets a stop. `finish` (2684-2780) only calls `pass_over` for those eight ends. `take_until_done` (2783-2799) stops only when `stopped()` is true. The three run-ending arms are Budget, JobLimit and Stop, which call `set_stop` at 2741, 2745 and 2749. Failed ends the run only through `StopCause` at 2729-2734, and that stays. What is missing is the one list, the exhaustiveness test, and a test per state that checks the next item lands. Plan: (1) in drain.rs add one macro-generated list, a pub fieldless `ItemEndKind` with `ALL` and `label()`, so the enum and `ALL` cannot drift apart. (2) Add `ItemEndKind::after()`, an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm that returns `AfterItem::Continues` or `AfterItem::EndsRun(Option<Stop>)`. (3) Add `ItemEnd::kind()`, also exhaustive. A new `ItemEnd` variant then fails to compile until it has a kind and an `after()`. (4) `finish` computes `after` first and sets the stop from the list after the match, in place of the three hand-written `set_stop` calls. The order is the same: `pass_over`, then `set_stop`. The Failed environment stop stays as it is. (5) In tests/drain.rs add four Stub knobs: `held`, `held_runs`, `unread` and `waiting_to_merge`. The Stub has no fields for those states today (Stub impl, tests/drain.rs:127-326). Add one `the_batch_goes_on_past_*` test per continuing state, all through `drain::drain`, each asserting that the next item `b` ran, landed and that the run ended `QueueEmpty`. Add two tests for the budget and job-limit stops after a skipped item. Add an exhaustiveness test that matches every `ItemEndKind` with no wildcard arm to the name of the test that drives it, and fails if that test fn is missing from the file. (6) Add a unit test in drain.rs that calls `finish` for a sample of every kind and checks the stop set agrees with `after()`. (7) Add a CHANGELOG entry and a new D190 in docs/decisions.md.

decisions.choice: One list: a macro in drain.rs that defines the pub `ItemEndKind` enum, its `ALL` array and its label from a single invocation. `after()` is an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm. `ItemEnd::kind()` is also an exhaustive match.
decisions.reason: `ItemEnd` is private and carries `String` payloads, so the integration test in tests/drain.rs cannot name it. A pub fieldless kind is visible to it, as `Stop::ALL` is (tests/drain.rs:2510). The macro removes the ALL-drift case where a variant is added to the enum but not to the array. Adding an `ItemEnd` variant breaks the build at `kind()`, then at `after()`, then at the test's exhaustive match. A new kind is therefore handled in code and in tests before anything compiles.

rejected.option: A hand-written `const ALL` array beside the enum, as `Stop::ALL` (drain.rs:1091)
rejected.why: A variant missing from the array is silent, and the request asks that adding a state without handling it must fail.
The enum is private to drain.rs, and tests/drain.rs is an integration test that sees only pub items.
It adds a dependency, and D173 requires a decision for each new one.

decisions.choice: `finish` takes its run-ending stops from the list: `AfterItem::EndsRun(Some(stop))` is Budget→BudgetSpent, JobLimit→JobLimit and Stop→Requested. Idle is `EndsRun(None)` because another worker already set the stop. Landed, Failed and the six other self-stopping ends are `Continues`.
decisions.reason: The list and the code then agree by construction, and a unit test checks it for every kind. Failed stays Continues because only an environment cause of its failure ends the run, through `StopCause` (drain.rs:2729-2734), which is the existing rule and out of scope. Behavior is unchanged: Budget, JobLimit and Stop still call `pass_over` and then `set_stop`.

rejected.option: A `debug_assert!` in `finish` that a continuing kind leaves `stop` unset
rejected.why: With parallel workers another worker may set a stop between the two reads, so the assert would be flaky.

rejected.option: Make `Failed` an `EndsRun` kind when its cause is environmental
rejected.why: That is failure-cause sorting, which the brief puts out of scope.

decisions.choice: The state and reason stay on the existing `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>` ui line (`pass_over`, drain.rs:1542-1550). `Report` and `display::drain` are not changed. The reason text of each arm already names its state: 'line a is paused', 'line a is flagged', 'awaiting diagnosis', 'failed twice', 'held:', 'not ready:', 'skipped:', 'waiting to merge'.
decisions.reason: Existing tests require the summary NOT to repeat the pass-over: tests/drain.rs:814 (`lift_mentions(&text, "a") == 0`) and 1062-1063 (summary lacks 'failed twice'). Changing the summary would break tests that must stay unchanged.

rejected.option: Add a passed-over list to `Report` and the summary
rejected.why: It breaks tests/drain.rs:814 and 1062-1063 and changes unrelated output.

decisions.choice: Exhaustiveness test in tests/drain.rs: for each kind in `ItemEndKind::ALL`, a no-wildcard `match` returns the name of the test that drives it. The test then asserts `include_str!("drain.rs")` contains `fn <name>(`, and that kinds whose `after()` is `Continues` and that are not Landed map to a `the_batch_goes_on_past_` test.
decisions.reason: A new variant fails to compile at the match. A deleted or renamed driving test fails at run time. Landed maps to `items_are_worked_in_plan_order_not_oldest_first`. Budget and JobLimit map to the new tests that follow a skipped item. Stop maps to `a_stop_asked_for_mid_run_finishes_the_current_job_and_starts_no_other` (tests/drain.rs:1382). Idle maps to `passed_over_item_is_logged_once_with_its_reason` (tests/drain.rs:6635; its 'run ended first' case for c at 6665).

rejected.why: It does not name which state lacks a test.

decisions.choice: Exit table of `Drain::finish`, with the exits of `Drain::attempts`. Each exit is listed with its handler, the state it leaves and the code that reads it next (take_until_done, drain.rs:2783-2799, reads `stopped()` and `queue`; the report reads `queued`, `jobs` and `stop`). Landed (attempts 2024-2026; finish 2686-2714): leaves the item landed and rebuilds and rates, and a rating or rebuild may set a stop that `stopped()` reads next. Failed (attempts 2050-2053; finish 2715-2735): leaves the item queued with a 'failed twice' pass-over line, and sets Stop::Environment only if `StopCause` is ProducerAuth or LowDisk. Budget (attempts 1982 and 2031; finish 2736-2742): pass-over, then Stop::BudgetSpent from the list, so `stopped()` ends the loop. JobLimit (attempts 1983; finish 2743-2746): pass-over, then Stop::JobLimit. Stop (attempts 1959; finish 2747-2750): pass-over, then Stop::Requested. Idle (attempts 1984; finish 2751-2753): pass-over only, because another worker already set the stop, so `stopped()` is already true. NeedsAccepting (attempts 1985; finish 2754-2760): pass-over 'not ready', and `stopped()` stays false so the next item is popped. Held (attempts 1986; finish 2761-2767): pass-over 'held:', no stop. Waiting (attempts 2029; finish 2768): pass-over 'waiting to merge', no stop. Paused (attempts 1964 and 2043; finish 2769-2771) and Flagged (attempts 2046) and Awaiting (attempts 1970 and 2051): pass-over with the scope guard's reason, no stop. Skipped (attempts 2000; finish 2772-2778): pass-over 'skipped:', no stop. Interrupt: a stop request is read at the job boundary (attempts 1958) and is the Stop exit above; a panic inside a worker is not changed by this plan. Error exits of `run_job` (unread reads, a run with no outcome) land in Skipped or Failed above.
decisions.reason: Required by the planner rules for a changed core flow. Only the three `set_stop` arms are edited; every other arm keeps its text.

files.purpose: Add the one list (`ItemEndKind` through a macro, with `ALL` and `label`), `AfterItem`, `ItemEndKind::after()` and `ItemEnd::kind()`, both exhaustive. `finish` takes the three run-ending stops from the list. Add the unit test `finish_agrees_with_the_item_end_list` to the existing test module.

Add the Stub knobs `held`, `held_runs`, `unread` and `waiting_to_merge`, eight `the_batch_goes_on_past_*` tests, two limit tests after a skipped item, and `every_end_of_an_item_has_a_test_that_drives_it`. Existing tests are unchanged.
Add an entry under [Unreleased] > Changed: the list, the exhaustiveness test, the per-state tests, that behavior is unchanged, and the limits.
Add a new entry D190 at the end. Existing entries are not edited.

steps: Read drain.rs 1423-1458 (ItemEnd), 2684-2780 (finish) and 1043-1149 (Stop with ALL, label and meaning) so the new list follows the same shape.

In drain.rs, near `ItemEnd`, add a macro `item_end_kinds!` that, from one invocation listing Landed, Failed, Budget, JobLimit, Stop, Idle, NeedsAccepting, Held, Skipped, Waiting, Paused, Flagged and Awaiting with a label each, defines the pub enum `ItemEndKind` (Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq), `ItemEndKind::ALL` and `ItemEndKind::label()`. Add `pub enum AfterItem { Continues, EndsRun(Option<Stop>) }` and `ItemEndKind::after()` as an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm: Budget → EndsRun(Some(BudgetSpent)), JobLimit → EndsRun(Some(JobLimit)), Stop → EndsRun(Some(Requested)), Idle → EndsRun(None), all others → Continues. Doc-comment that Landed is Continues, that Failed is Continues apart from the `StopCause` environment stop, and that adding an `ItemEnd` variant breaks the build here on purpose. Add `ItemEnd::kind()` as an exhaustive match. Update the `ItemEnd` and module docs to point at the list.

In `finish`, compute `let after = end.kind().after();` before the match, drop the three `self.set_stop(..)` calls in the Budget, JobLimit and Stop arms (keeping their `pass_over` calls), and add after the match `if let AfterItem::EndsRun(Some(stop)) = after { self.set_stop(stop); }`. Leave the Landed arm and the Failed environment check unchanged. Keep `ItemEndKind` and `AfterItem` pub so tests/drain.rs can use them.

In tests/drain.rs add to `Stub`: `held: Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)>` (returned by a new `Steps::held` override that filters by the jobs asked about, like `flagged`), `held_runs: Vec<&'static str>` (`run` returns `Run { held: true, reason: "budget short: ...", outcome: None, .. }` for those jobs), `unread: Vec<&'static str>` (`read` returns `Read { job: Some(job), error: Some("the reader gave no reading"), runnable: false, .. }` for `ReadOf::Queued` of those jobs), and `waiting_to_merge: Vec<&'static str>` (`land` returns `Landing::Waiting("checks have not finished")`). Add `hold_text(line)` beside `pause_text` and `flag_text`, wording the reason with 'awaiting diagnosis'. Add the helper `assert_batch_continues(kind, stub, state_text, reason_text)` using `Stamped`, and the eight `the_batch_goes_on_past_*` tests (a paused item, a flagged item, an item awaiting diagnosis, an item that failed twice, a held item, an item that needs accepting, a skipped item, an item waiting to merge).

In tests/drain.rs add `the_batch_goes_on_past_a_skipped_item_only_while_slots_remain` (max_jobs 3, expecting Stop::JobLimit with c passed over as 'over the job limit') and `the_batch_goes_on_past_a_skipped_item_only_while_budget_remains` (a budget chosen by running the test and noted in a comment, expecting Stop::BudgetSpent). Add `every_end_of_an_item_has_a_test_that_drives_it`, with the no-wildcard match from `ItemEndKind` to a test name and an `include_str!("drain.rs")` check for `fn <name>(`; Landed, Budget, JobLimit, Stop and Idle map to the tests listed in the decisions.

In the test module of drain.rs add `sample(kind: ItemEndKind) -> ItemEnd` (exhaustive) and the unit test `finish_agrees_with_the_item_end_list`. It checks that `sample(kind).kind() == kind`, that labels are non-empty and distinct, that `ALL` has 13 entries, and that after `Drain::new(&stub, &Quiet, caps, limits)` and `finish(&item, sample(kind))` the stop equals `after()` (Landed run apart, with rating 3 below the target of 4).

Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] > Changed: the request, the finding that the drain already continued past each state (with file:line), the list and its compile-time and run-time checks, the new tests, limits (a sample of the stop timing is not measured with parallel workers; the summary is unchanged by design), and the D190 reference. Add D190 at the end of docs/decisions.md in D189's layout, without the phrases 'Amends' or 'Supersedes'.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, then `cargo test --locked`, and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain the_batch_goes_on_past_` on its own. Also do the one-arm mutation check from criterion 5 and revert it before finishing, and say so in the report.

risks.risk: The request reads as if the drain stops today, but the code already continues for all eight states, so a reader may expect a behavior change.
risks.mitigation: State plainly in the CHANGELOG and D190 that the drain already continued past each state (drain.rs:2036-2053 and 2684-2778) and that the change adds the one list and the tests. The request's 'make it the default' therefore needs no production behavior change, and the producer must not invent one.

risks.risk: The budget-limit test's budget value is brittle, because it depends on the stub costs and caps (tests/drain.rs:39 and 128-134) and on `Budget::fits`.
risks.mitigation: The producer sets the number by running the test, keeps a comment showing the sum (a's two reads at 0.1 each, b's read 0.1, run 0.5 and rating 0.2, against c's read and run caps of 1.2), and asserts `Stop::BudgetSpent` exactly. The job-limit variant is deterministic.

risks.risk: Criterion 5 (the tests fail if the pass-over stops the run) cannot be shown by the verifier, who has no command that edits the tree.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs the real tree, then states in its report which arm it mutated and which test failed.

risks.risk: The macro could trip clippy or make the list harder to grep.
risks.mitigation: A macro with plain `$v:ident => $label:literal` arms, `#[allow]` only if clippy asks, and docs on the generated items. Run clippy locally before finishing.

risks.risk: Calling `finish(Landed)` in the unit test runs `rebuild_if_due` and `rate`, which could set a stop and confuse the agreement check.
risks.mitigation: The unit test skips Landed's stop check and runs it separately with a rating of 3 against the target of 4, as `tests::Stub` does (drain.rs:5028-5034), so the rate step sets no stop.

risks.risk: The D187 gate checks new statement-opening phrases in docs/decisions.md for links that no one adds.
risks.mitigation: D190 avoids those phrases. If the D187 gate still wants a link, the producer reports it, because docs/decision-links.toml is not a deliverable.

demonstrations.method: Eight tests, one per continuing state, each building a Stub with items a and b and driving a into one state. Paused: `paused: [("a", pause_text("a"))]`. Flagged: outcomes Rejected, Rejected, Landed plus `flagged: [("a", flag_text("a"))]`. Awaiting: new `held: [("a", <text with 'awaiting diagnosis'>)]`. Failed twice: outcomes Rejected, Rejected, Landed with no flag. Held: new `held_runs: ["a"]`, so `run` returns `held: true` with reason 'budget short: ...'. Needs accepting: `needs_accepting: ["a"]`. Skipped: new `unread: ["a"]`, so the read gives an error twice. Waiting: new `waiting_to_merge: ["a"]`, so `land` returns `Landing::Waiting`. A shared helper runs `drain::drain` with the `Stamped` ui and asserts: exactly one line starting `plan       a passed over:` containing the state text and the reason; `report.jobs` has b with outcome 'passed' and landing 'landed'; the log has `run b` and `land b` after a's own calls; `report.landed == 1`; `report.stop == Stop::QueueEmpty`; and the helper asserts the kind's `after()` is `Continues`.
demonstrations.observes: Each state yields one pass-over line with job a, the state and the reason, then b runs and lands, and the run ends QueueEmpty.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the arm of `finish` for that state called `set_stop`, or `attempts` returned a run-ending end, `b` would not run: `stub.log()` would lack `run b` and `land b`, `report.landed` would be 0 and the stop would not be QueueEmpty, so the test fails.

The stub returns scripted inputs only; the continue-or-stop logic under test is the production `Drain`.
